opening_message:
Ticket 1: Diana Cooper (employee ID E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E020.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Diana Cooper (E020) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Source Code. Since Engineers own Source Code, full-time employees in the owning role may have admin. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Engineer
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Diana Cooper (E020) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never exceed read without advanced training. Requested admin is above the maximum, so grant read.
reason: There is conflicting information about Diana Cooper's employment type. HR notes list her as full-time Engineer (which would allow admin for Source Code since Engineers own it), but the Security DB shows she is a contractor with only basic security training. Under policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read access, never admin. Since the requested admin level exceeds the contractor maximum, and the Security record is the authoritative source for access decisions, the maximum permissible level is read.
